chunks: Sama‘ah ibn Mihran informed me; he said: Al-Kalbī the genealogist informed me; he said:

I entered al-Madinah while knowing nothing of this matter. I came to the mosque, and there was a group from Quraysh there. I said: Tell me about the learned one of the people of this House. They said: ‘Abd Allah ibn al-Hasan. So I went to his house and sought permission. A man came out to me, and I thought he was his servant, so I said to him: Seek permission for me to enter upon your master. He went in, then came out and said to me: Enter. I entered, and there was an old man in retreat, intense in exertion. I greeted him, and he said to me: Who are you? I said: I am al-Kalbī the genealogist. He said: What is your need? I said: I have come to ask you. He said: Did you pass by my son Muhammad? I said: I began with you. He said: Ask.

So I said: Tell me about a man who says to his wife: You are divorced by the number of the stars of the sky. He said: She becomes separated at the head of al-Jawza’, and the rest is a burden and punishment upon him. I said to myself: One. Then I said: What does the shaykh say regarding wiping over the khuffs? He said: Righteous people have wiped, but we, the Ahl al-Bayt, do not wipe. I said to myself: Two. Then I said: What do you say regarding eating al-jirrī — is it halal or haram? He said: It is halal, except that we, the Ahl al-Bayt, find it repugnant. I said to myself: Three. Then I said: What do you say regarding drinking nabīdh? He said: It is halal, except that we, the Ahl al-Bayt, do not drink it. So I stood and left his presence saying: This group lies against the people of this House.

Then I entered the mosque and looked at a group of Quraysh and others from among the people. I greeted them, then said to them: Who is the most learned of the people of this House? They said: ‘Abd Allah ibn al-Hasan. I said: I have gone to him, but I found nothing with him. Then a man from the group raised his head and said: Go to Ja‘far ibn Muhammad عليه السلام, for he is the most learned of the people of this House. Some of those present reproached him. I said: Nothing prevented the people from guiding me to him the first time except envy. Then I said to him: Woe to you — he is the one I wanted.

So I went until I came to his house and knocked at the door. A servant of his came out and said: Enter, O brother of Kalb. By Allah, that astonished me. I entered while disturbed, and I looked and there was an old man on a prayer place without cushion or saddle-cloth. After I greeted him, he initiated and said to me: Who are you? I said to myself: Glory be to Allah — his servant said to me at the door, Enter, O brother of Kalb, while the master asks me: Who are you? So I said to him: I am al-Kalbī the genealogist.

He struck his hand on his forehead and said: Those who set up equals with Allah have lied, gone far astray, and suffered a manifest loss. O brother of Kalb, indeed Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says: “And ‘Ad and Thamud and the companions of al-Rass and many generations between that.” Can you trace their lineages? I said: No, may I be made your ransom. He said to me: Can you trace your own lineage? I said: Yes, I am so-and-so son of so-and-so son of so-and-so, until I went up the line. He said to me: Stop — it is not as you are going. Woe to you — do you know who so-and-so son of so-and-so was? I said: Yes, so-and-so son of so-and-so.

He said: So-and-so son of so-and-so was the son of so-and-so, the Kurdish shepherd. That Kurdish shepherd had been on the mountain of the family of so-and-so, then he descended to so-and-so, the wife of so-and-so, from his mountain upon which he used to pasture his sheep. He fed her something and approached her, and she gave birth to so-and-so. And so-and-so son of so-and-so was from so-and-so woman and so-and-so son of so-and-so. Then he said: Do you recognize these names? I said: No, by Allah, may I be made your ransom. If you see fit to refrain from this, then do so. He said: It was only because you spoke. I said: I shall not return to it. He said: Then we shall not return to it; ask about what you came for.

So I said to him: Tell me about a man who says to his wife: You are divorced by the number of the stars of the sky. He said: Woe to you, do you not read Surat al-Talaq? I said: Yes. He said: Then read. So I read: “Then divorce them for their prescribed period and keep count of the prescribed period.” He said: Do you see here the stars of the sky? I said: No.

I said: Then what of a man who says to his wife: You are divorced three times? He said: It is referred back to the Book of Allah and the sunnah of His Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله. Then he said: There is no divorce except in a state of purity without intercourse, with two acceptable witnesses. I said to myself: One. Then he said: Ask. I said: What do you say regarding wiping over the khuffs? He smiled, then said: When it is the Day of Resurrection and Allah returns everything to its proper thing, and returns the skin to the sheep, then you will see where the wudu of those who wipe will go. I said to myself: Two.

Then he turned to me and said: Ask. So I said: Tell me about eating al-jirrī. He said: Allah, Mighty and Majestic, transformed a group from the Children of Israel; whatever the sea took from them is al-jirrī, al-mārmāhī, al-zimmār, and what is besides that; and whatever the land took from them is the monkeys, the pigs, the hyrax, the warak, and what is besides that. I said to myself: Three.

Then he turned to me and said: Ask, and rise. I said: What do you say regarding nabīdh? He said: It is halal. I said: We prepare nabīdh, putting into it sediment and other such things, and we drink it. He said: Shh, shh — that is the foul wine. I said: May I be made your ransom, then which nabīdh do you mean? He said: The people of al-Madinah complained to the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله about the change in the water and the corruption of their constitutions, so he ordered them to prepare nabīdh. A man would command his servant to prepare it for him, and he would take a handful of dates and cast it into the water-skin. From it was his drink and from it was his means of purification. I said: How many dates were in the handful? He said: Whatever the palm held. I said: One or two? He said: Sometimes it was one and sometimes it was two. I said: How much would the water-skin hold? He said: Between forty and eighty and beyond that. I said: In ratls? He said: Yes, ratls by the measure of Iraq.

Sama‘ah said: Al-Kalbī said: Then he عليه السلام rose, and I rose, and I left striking one hand upon the other, saying: If there is anything, then this is it. And al-Kalbī continued to worship Allah through love of the family of this House until he died.

key_terms.أَهْلِ هَذَا الْبَيْتِ: the household of the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم, presented here as the locus of true knowledge
key_terms.الطَّلَاقِ: divorce, discussed in relation to its valid conditions according to revelation
key_terms.النَّبِيذِ: date-infused drink, distinguished here from intoxicating wine
key_terms.الْأَمْرِ: the matter of wilayah and rightful religious authority
key_terms.الْجِرِّيِّ: a type of fish discussed here under halal and haram rulings
key_terms.الْمَسْحِ عَلَى الْخُفَّيْنِ: wiping over leather footwear in wudu (ablution)
key_terms.حُبِّ آلِ هَذَا الْبَيْتِ: love of the family of this House as a basis of religious devotion
key_terms.سُنَّةِ نَبِيِّهِ: the normative Prophetic sunnah as a source for legal judgment

ai.seo_question: How does this hadith show Imam Ja‘far al-Sadiq عليه السلام as the most knowledgeable of Ahl al-Bayt in matters of law and authority?
ai.summary: This narration recounts how al-Kalbī sought the most learned member of Ahl al-Bayt and, after disappointment with another claimant, came to Imam Ja‘far ibn Muhammad عليه السلام. Through answers on divorce, wudu (ablution), halal and haram foods, and nabīdh, as well as a striking demonstration of hidden knowledge, the report presents the Imam عليه السلام as the true religious authority whose guidance accords with the Book of Allah and the sunnah of the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم.
